newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends lower in quiet June expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends lower in quiet June expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed slightly lower on Thursday amid an uneventful June contract expiry, traders said.

The June contract expired some seven cents lower at $19.44 a barrel, while the July contract settled five cents off at $19.49. "It was a very quiet expiry. A fair number of people were trading the June/July spread level but that was about it," said one trader.

Traders said Brent futures were in rangebound mood for most of the session as strong technicals counterbalanced the effect of recent bearish supply statistics, run cuts and an average June Brent loading programme.

Players said news Texaco was cutting crude runs at their Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam by 10 percent over the whole of May had dented prices early on.The company controls 35 percent of the 400,000 bpd complex.
A number of traders had hoped for some support from a lower than usual June Brent loading programme, but it was little changed at 38.4 cargoes in June against 41.8 cargoes in May.

Many traders were still holding out for a recovery soon, saying June Brent's action at the end of last week and Monday which saw it fill a key capping gap and push above stubborn trendline resistance had left firm technical support.
June gas oil ended its session $1.25 higher at $172.00 a tonne. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
